text:
ajay: ran the benchmark that mixes synthetic and 24h replay to validate the new kernel-selection heuristic. summary below, hit some strange KV priming behavior.

maria: very curious — did you pin model + seq len distribution?

ajay: yup pinned gptx-7b-v2, seq=1024 for synthetic and replay was filtered to same seq distribution. batches sampled to match 95th percentile shapes.

sasha: what heuristic did you try? last time we overshot batch sizes and saw token-latency tail.

ajay: new heuristic picks kernel based on predicted effective batchshape histogram instead of instantaneous batch size. it uses a small moving window (20ms) of arriving shapes. goal is fewer kernel switches during bursts so warmup overhead drops.

lee: nice. what about KV cache warmup? replay should have much higher prefix hits, synthetic not.

ajay: exactly. we measured KV hit-rate and added a priming pass for the replay runs to simulate ongoing sessions. without priming: KV hit 12% (replay), with priming: 78%. interestingly, the kernel heuristic interacts with priming: when priming is low, we choose smaller-kernel path -> worse throughput under burst.

ajay: quick numbers (steady 2m window, p50/p95 token-latency, throughput tokens/s):
```
scenario                p50   p95   tps   kv_hit
replay+priming+heur     65ms  210ms  8200  78%
replay+priming+baseline 70ms  260ms  7300  78%
synthetic+heur          72ms  320ms  6400  12%
synthetic+baseline      68ms  280ms  6900  12%
```

maria: wow p95 difference on synthetic is big. looks like kernel switching slowed tails. any profiling?

ajay: attached flame samples from gpu-prof and our runtime trace. main culprit: kernel warmup (~7–12ms per switch) plus extra memcpy for some quant paths. also noticed quant-kernel v2.1 fallback path had a 1.8x stall in warp occupancy on A100.

sasha: so heuristic helps replay workloads (because KV priming keeps larger batches consistent) but hurts synthetic where shapes vary widely. tradeoff.

lee: for apples-to-apples we should ensure the prefix cache state is identical across runs. can we pre-warm KV to the same hit-rate?

ajay: did that for the replay+priming row. for synthetic i tried two modes: unprimed (realistic) and artificially-primed (to test kernel steady-state). both included in full log.

infra-bot: benchmark job completed: https://dash.redwood.internal/runs/789 (artifacts + profiles) :white_check_mark:

maria: what's the scale-up/coldstart story? autoscale metrics?

ajay: good question. scale-up measured using dedicated pool with burst credits disabled vs enabled:
```
case                         coldstart(ms) scale-up(s) burst_used
dedicated/no-burst           420ms         34s         0
dedicated/with-burst         420ms         9s          3 credits
hosted/ephemeral             560ms         52s         n/a
```
note: coldstart here = first-token latency from zero KV state right after new worker spinup; scale-up = time to reach 90% of steady tps.

sasha: 9s with burst credits is solid. are we seeing regressions after kernel changes? any perf regressions vs last release?

ajay: regression: quant-kernel 2.1 introduced memcpy ordering change that increases p95 under certain seq shapes by ~12% on synthetic. replay runs masked it because KV priming keeps batchshape stable. filing bug.

maria: action items?

ajay: 1) revert memcpy ordering in quant-kernel 2.1 for next canary, 2) add a config toggle to prefer stability-over-peak in kernel heuristic (opt-in per route), 3) extend benchmark harness to inject controlled KV hit-rates so we can sweep priming levels, 4) reproduce scale-up with dedicated pool under churn (50% worker churn).

sasha: also add a metric: kernel-switch-rate per-second and correlate with p95. that should help quantize tradeoffs.

lee: +1 on controlled KV sweep. i can wire a flag in the replay harness to toggle prefill ratio.

ajay: pushing a branch with results and raw profiles here: https://git.redwood.internal/runtime/bench/branch/heur-priming (PR coming). please review before EOD.

maria: I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow to choose canary config. thanks ajay :thumbsup:

sasha: can we also run one dedicated pool test with autoscaler disabled to validate baseline steady-state? often autoscaler masks regressions.

ajay: yep will add that to the test matrix. tracking in the ticket: RUNTIME-1129.
